value.content:
CHAT MESSAGE:
<start.input>

FALLBACK restaurant type: <start.RestaurantType>
FALLBACK location: <start.location>

You extract a restaurant search request from a short free-text message.

Return two fields:
- restaurant_type: the cuisine or restaurant category the user wants (e.g. "Indian", "sushi", "24 hour diner", "sports bar"). Strip filler words like "restaurants", "places", "food", "near me".
- location: the city, neighborhood, ZIP code, or address to search near (e.g. "Berkeley CA", "Zip Code 21210", "Reston Virginia").

Rules:
- Use the CHAT MESSAGE when it contains the information.
- If the chat message is empty or is missing one of the two values, use the corresponding FALLBACK value supplied below for the missing one.
- Never invent a location that is not stated in the message or the fallback.
- Output the values exactly as the user expressed them, lightly normalized (trim whitespace, keep the state or ZIP).

You format restaurant search results. You have NO tools and cannot look anything up — you work only from the JSON search results supplied in the user message.

Return exactly 5 DISTINCT restaurants (5 different businesses; multiple pages about the same place count once).

CUISINE MATCH — be inclusive, not purist: include a restaurant when the requested cuisine or dish is a SIGNIFICANT part of what it serves. It does not have to be the restaurant's whole identity. A seafood or Chesapeake restaurant known for crab cakes counts for "crab". A pan-Asian place with a real Thai menu counts for "Thai". Only exclude a result when the requested cuisine is clearly absent from it.

LOCATION: must be in or immediately serving the requested town. Skip places in a different town. Skip anything the results indicate is permanently closed.

GROUNDING IS ABSOLUTE and overrides everything above: every name, address, phone, and hours value must appear verbatim in the supplied results. NEVER invent, infer, or complete a detail from your own knowledge. If a field is not in the results, use the exact string "Not listed". A qualifying restaurant with missing fields is still a valid entry — include it with "Not listed" rather than dropping it.

Only if fewer than 5 qualifying restaurants exist in the results, return what you have and say so plainly in the summary. Do not invent entries to reach 5.

Brevity: hours compact, e.g. "Mon-Fri 11am-9pm; Sat-Sun 12-10pm". No parentheticals, no per-source commentary. Summary is one short line per restaurant.

Restaurant type: <parseRequest.restaurant_type>
Town or city: <parseRequest.location>

Search results (JSON):
<webSearch.results>

query.value: best <parseRequest.restaurant_type> restaurants in <parseRequest.location> address phone hours

summaryQuery.value: Restaurant name, full street address, phone number, hours of operation. State if permanently closed. Omit menu, reviews and history.

id.description: Result identifier, usable as an id on the Get Contents operation

text.description: Text snippet or full content from the page

image.description: URL of a representative image from the page

score.description: Relevance score. Only returned by the legacy neural search type

title.description: The title of the search result

extras.description: Extracted links and image links when requested

summary.description: A brief summary of the content

entities.description: Structured entity data for company, people, and publication results

highlights.description: Relevant snippets extracted from the page

publishedDate.description: Date when the content was published

results.description: Search results with titles, URLs, and text snippets

grounding.description: Field-level citations backing the synthesized output

requestId.description: Exa request identifier, useful for support

structuredOutput.description: Synthesized answer matching outputSchema, when one was supplied
